column2: req_desc

Keyboard diff cursor
The diff moves between files and lines by keyboard with the published keys, every diff row announces itself with its published name, and the cursor row holds focus.

Comment dialog by keyboard
A reviewer opens a line comment with the comment key, submits it with Ctrl+Enter or cancels it with Escape, focus stays inside the dialog while it is open and returns to the cursor row when it closes.

Request changes from keyboard review
A reviewer opens the review dialog with the review key and requests changes with a summary, and every open merge box then lists the changes-requested rule and announces it.

Check report clears rule live
A runner's success report for a required check removes the checks rule from every open merge box within the live update delay.

Suggestions on line comments
A comment on new-side lines may carry replacement lines for exactly its line range, shown with Apply suggestion and Add to batch controls.

Apply one or a batch
Applying one suggestion or a batch makes exactly one new revision with the published message and replaces the lines in the diff.

Stale suggestion refused
A suggestion whose lines changed since it was made is refused with the published message, and a batch containing one applies nothing.

New comments arrive live
A new comment appears on every open copy of the change within the live update delay, is announced, and animates in only when motion is allowed.

Dismissal follows the diff
A push dismisses an approval only when the change's combined diff differs from the diff that was approved, and a dismissed approval shows the published text and its merge-box rule at once.

Threads follow new revisions
After a new head revision a thread on an unchanged line moves to its new line number and a thread on a changed or removed line becomes outdated with its history kept, and outdated threads show only when the switch is on.

Viewed marks and derived counts
A file marked viewed resets when a later revision changes that file's head content, and the files viewed, unresolved threads and approvals remaining counts always equal values recomputed from the records.

Thread and viewed keys
The thread and viewed keys move between unresolved visible threads and toggle viewed for the cursor's file, and the counts update live.

Restack with the file-level rule
When a change gets a new revision every change above it is restacked in stack order with the file-level apply rule into a revision with the published message.

Restack keeps approvals
A restack that leaves a change's combined diff identical keeps its approvals and viewed marks, and a restack that changes the diff dismisses them.

Restack conflict stops the stack
A restack that conflicts stops at that change with the published notice, marks every change above it as not restacked, and gives none of them a new revision.

Restack results announced
Every restack result is announced in the Review updates region, in stack order, with the published sentences.

Owners file matching
Code owners are matched by path from the owners file with the published glob rules, and the last matching line wins.

Owner approvals in the merge box
Every changed path with owners needs a current approval from one of its owners, and the merge box lists the paths still waiting in byte order.

Owners come from the base revision
Owners are read from the base revision, so a change's own edits to the owners file never change who must approve.

Code-owner journey to enabled merge
As owners approve in separate sessions the code-owners rule shrinks live until the merge button becomes enabled.

Check reports
A repository token reports a check state for a revision and a name, only the latest report counts, and the published errors apply.

Check timeout edge
A required check without a final report is still in progress one second before the published timeout, is timed out at the timeout itself, and refuses later reports.

Check rows live
Check rows and the checks rule update live with the exact state words, and the browser never decides a time-dependent state.

Server clock route
The grading clock route advances the one server clock and answers only after every due timer has fired and its updates have been pushed.

Stack panel
A change based on another change's head branch appears in the stack panel from bottom to top with its number and position.

Restack order in a three-change stack
A push to the bottom change restacks the middle and top changes in order, and a conflict in the middle stops the top.

Approval carry-over rail
The stack rail walks up from the change above the updated change, expanding each row in turn and settling with the published result word and attributes, and the results persist after reload.

Rail keyboard and reduced motion
Arrow keys move between rail rows, Enter opens a row's change, and with reduced motion every row shows its result at once.

Merge is atomic
Merging advances the base branch and marks the change merged together or not at all, with the published merge revision.

Retarget after a lower merge
When a lower change merges, the next change is retargeted to the lower change's base branch and restacked with the published notice.

Merge mail
A merged change mails its author with the published subject, sender and change header.

Queue step merges the head
The merge queue merges the head entry at a server-clock step once every required check has passed on its queue revision.

Queue revisions
Each queue entry has a queue revision made of the base head, the entries ahead of it and itself, and its required checks are judged on that revision.

Removal reasons and reset
A removed entry records its own published reason and every entry behind it gets a new queue revision with its checks reset.

Live queue positions
Queue positions, states and removal reasons update live on the queue page and are announced.

Failing middle entry journey
When the middle of three entries fails its check it is removed, the third is re-checked, and the head still merges at the next queue step.

Queue reorder
A maintainer reorders entries by keyboard or buttons, and the moved entries and those behind them get new queue revisions.

Queue entry timeout removal
A head entry whose required check never reports is removed when the server clock passes the check timeout.

Queue admission refusals
A draft change, a change with unmet rules and every other ineligible change is refused from the queue with the published messages.

Queue steps
One queue step merges at most the head entry, steps follow the server clock, and entries merge in queue order.

Push API and error order
The push route creates one revision, and every API answers its errors in the published order with the published bodies.

One winner for concurrent saves
Of two simultaneous saves with the same expected head exactly one revision is kept and the other is refused as stale.

Retried push
A push retried with the same expected head after it succeeded is refused as stale and creates no second revision.

Editor keeps typed text
A browser save refused for a stale head shows the published notice with a Load latest button and keeps the typed text.

Phone diff layout
Below the diff breakpoint only the unified view shows, the file tree sits in the Files drawer, and the page never scrolls sideways.

Review by touch
On a phone a reviewer taps a row, comments through that row's comment button and approves from the review dialog.

Live merge box on phone
A check report reaches the merge box on a phone live, with controls at least 44 px.

Widening restores split
Widening the viewport to the diff breakpoint brings back the split view with the same row attributes.

Row accessible names
Every diff row's accessible name follows the published pattern for added, removed, unchanged and empty lines.

Review updates region
Review, check, restack, queue, merge and comment events are announced in one status region with the published sentences.

Dialog focus
Comment, review and dismissal dialogs keep Tab inside themselves, close on Escape and return focus to their opener.

Line diff output
The diff is a minimal line diff with the published tie-break, context and hunk headers.

Reader limits
A reader can read and comment but cannot approve or request changes, shown disabled with its reason in the UI and refused with 403 in the API.

Private repositories answer not found
Every change, revision, file and thread of a repository the caller cannot see answers not found, by address and as the not-found page, never forbidden and never invalid.

Maintainer dismisses a review
A maintainer dismisses a request-changes review with a reason, the review shows the published text, and the changes-requested rule drops live.

Repository administration
Maintainers and owners manage merge rules, tokens and role grants, and organisations and teams exist so owners can be teams.

Change mail
Review requests, mentions and merges send mail through a durable outbox with the published subjects, sender and change header.

Sign-up confirmation mail
Signing up sends a confirmation mail and the account can log in only after the link is used.

Archive export
Exporting a revision writes a zip to storage with the published entries and shows it saved only after storage confirms it.

Stored bytes and storage outage
Pushed files are stored exactly as submitted, and while storage is down pushes, browser edits and exports are refused with the published outage copy.

Working screens
The inbox, repositories, repository overview, file view, revision view, change creation and review-request screens show the published content and controls.

Platform and boundary
The app starts from the run manifest, answers health, reads every credential and limit from the environment and obeys the server boundary.

Visual language
Every screen uses one near-black language where light on a control means it changes the base branch.

Signed-out home
The signed-out home shows the two-column hero with a five-slab wireframe, the revision player and the bento cards with invented repositories.

Responsive and tap targets
Every screen fits 375, 768 and 1280 pixel widths without sideways scroll, with controls at least 44 px below 1024 pixels.

Motion and reduced motion
Every motion has the published meaning and duration range, no unnamed loop runs, and reduced motion shows final states with no movement.

Source integrity
The source shows real service wiring, no AI, no fake state, no external assets and each domain rule decided in one place.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and the commands run on a fresh checkout.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package and bundled font with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree.
Every shipped package is licensed MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC or 0BSD, and the bundled fonts are OFL-1.1.
The only datastores and services are the provided Postgres, MinIO and Mailpit: no other database, cache, queue or search engine, no git executable or library, and no AI or model service.
Pages load no outside host at runtime; fonts, icons and artwork are bundled files or generated in the page.

Every service credential and URL named in Configuration and secrets is read from the environment and appears in no source file or browser bundle as a literal; APP_PUBLIC_PORT and every variable in the defaults table there are read from the environment, with their published defaults and the 4173 port fallback written as configuration defaults only in the single place in the server source that reads the configuration; the string defaults of GRADING_KEY, WORKSPACE_TIME_ZONE and MAIL_FROM never appear in the browser bundle, the browser takes DIFF_BREAKPOINT_PX from the value the server serves with each page, and numeric literals in CSS, motion timings and incidental bundled code do not count as configuration defaults.
The provided service configuration and its seeded users, bucket and database are left untouched; the app creates its own tables and objects idempotently.
